html:
The Jesuit missionary Francis Xavier landed at Kagoshima in southern Japan in August 1549 and spent just over two years in the country. He started the first Christian mission there.

Xavier had worked in India from Goa and in Malacca, where he met a Japanese man named Anjirō who became a Christian and guided him to Japan. Japan was then split among warring lords. Xavier travelled to Hirado, Yamaguchi and Kyoto, hoping to win over the emperor, but the capital was in ruins and the emperor powerless. He found that gifts and good dress opened doors with local lords. He left in 1551 and died the next year off the coast of China.

The Jesuits who followed him used the Nanban trade to win the favour of lords. Within fifty years Japan had perhaps 300,000 Christians, centred on Kyushu and Nagasaki. Then rulers turned against the faith: Hideyoshi ordered missionaries out in 1587, and the Tokugawa banned Christianity in 1614. After the Shimabara Rebellion the remaining believers went underground.
sum: The Jesuit missionary Francis Xavier landed at Kagoshima in southern Japan in August 1549 and spent just over two years in the country. He started the first Christian mission there.
